email.body1:
Ryan, saw Paystand launched USDb, the first stablecoin built for commercial enterprise finance, on the back of the Bitwage acquisition.

A launch that ambitious usually opens more accounts in play than the team can cover before the motion ramps, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Paystand off hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?

Ryan, quick follow-up for Paystand.

With USDb and Bitwage expanding the footprint, targets usually climb faster than the team can cover. Most teams cannot say how many meetings they need to hit the number, so the gap surfaces late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Paystand needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.

Ryan, last bit of proof for Paystand.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Paystand's reply rate likely compares to other fintech teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
